title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Home for the rulings: plans/c201-session-tiers-rulings.md on this branch, then docs/decisions/session-tiers.md (part L0, a records lane writing it). Summary: one coordinator per repo; triage always a standing session; a batch runner as a third standing role (shiv's word "branch manager"), the three started together by the coordinator before any lane; triage and the batch runner rotate before they go stale, started by the coordinator itself and archived only after draining (coordinator succession dropped, Oct 28 15:24); a session pushes back in one line when work reaches the wrong tier; shape is picked from the request (solo, one lane, coordinator). Rulings, Oct 28 16:15 CDT (shiv, waiting page): item 50 b, lane sessions run Opus (they keep themselves light but need top reasoning on what they are asked); item 53 a, test the cloud route for a per-tier context limit (his step, item 58, done Oct 28 17:46 CDT: he says the variable works in an experimental cloud session he made; unverified by a session of ours until the coordinator starts a lane there and reads its limit). Ruling, Oct 28 17:50 CDT (shiv, item 59, a): keep today's helper-agent model and effort table until lane L1 measures cost and quality. Open: whether he answers triage directly more often. Lanes L1 (rules, glossary), L2 (skills), L3 (session-start guard) start after batch 13 merges. Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28).
